claim: An input-dependent (dynamic) CNS gate lowers held-out loss compared with the static per-channel gate, for a real-wiring core with learned Dale-preserving edges on the frozen v3 trunk.

protocol.notes: 3,000-type subgraph (synapse-mass core + proportional inputs/outputs; 629,875 edges): the per-token persistent scan costs ~4x a reset step, which the full graph cannot afford here. 2 of every 8 rows are synthetic temporal-memory rows (recall at a distance, pattern, count, first item) in every arm.

notes: The dynamic-gate effect was first seen in the exploratory X-CNS-001 run (seed 1: pooled -0.0077 nats/char, temporal 6.78 -> 2.60) before this file was written; seed 1 is therefore excluded and the confirmation uses seeds 2-4. Same protocol as H-CNS-003 / X-CNS-001 (3,000-type subgraph, learned Dale edges, 250 core-only steps). Confirmatory test of the exploratory finding; threshold 1% of the static arm's pooled nats/char (the exploratory effect was 1.8%).
